mcq.explanation: Gonococcus (Neisseria gonorrhoeae), Vibrio cholerae, and Pseudomonas are all oxidase positive bacteria. The oxidase test is used to identify bacteria that produce cytochrome oxidase.

mcq.q: Treponema pallidum can be cultivated in
mcq.explanation: Treponema pallidum is cultivated in rabbit testes as it does not grow in standard culture media. This method is used for research and for maintaining the organism for diagnostic purposes.

mcq.q: Pathogenicity of Neisseria gonorrhoeae is due to
mcq.explanation: Pili (fimbriae) allow Neisseria gonorrhoeae to attach to mucosal surfaces and evade the host immune response, contributing significantly to pathogenicity. They mediate adhesion and resistance to phagocytosis.

mcq.q: Nichol's strain of Treponema pallidum is maintained in
mcq.explanation: The Nichol's strain of Treponema pallidum is maintained in the testis of rabbits for experimental purposes. This strain is used in research on syphilis.

mcq.q: Which of the following is the causative agent of donovanosis? (PG Entrance 2020)
mcq.explanation: Donovanosis (granuloma inguinale) is caused by Klebsiella granulomatis (formerly Calymmatobacterium granulomatis). It is a chronic, granulomatous infection of the genital region.

mcq.q: Inclusion conjunctivitis is caused by
mcq.explanation: Inclusion conjunctivitis is caused by Chlamydia trachomatis (serotypes D-K). It is a sexually transmitted infection that can cause conjunctivitis in newborns and adults.

mcq.q: The most common cause of otitis externa is
mcq.explanation: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is the most common cause of otitis externa (swimmer's ear). It is an opportunistic pathogen that thrives in moist environments.

mcq.q: Which of the following is the most common cause of otitis media in children?
mcq.explanation: Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, and Moraxella catarrhalis are the most common causes of otitis media in children. They are the major pathogens responsible for acute otitis media.

mcq.q: Swimming pool conjunctivitis is caused by
mcq.explanation: Adenovirus is a common cause of "swimming-pool conjunctivitis." It is transmitted through contaminated water and causes acute follicular conjunctivitis.

mcq.q: Keratoconjunctivitis caused by adenovirus is also known as
mcq.explanation: Adenoviral keratoconjunctivitis is also known as swimming pool conjunctivitis. It is transmitted through contaminated water and causes acute follicular conjunctivitis.

mcq.q: Ophthalmia neonatorum is most commonly caused by
mcq.explanation: Chlamydia trachomatis is the most common cause of ophthalmia neonatorum (neonatal conjunctivitis). It is transmitted to the newborn during delivery through the birth canal.

mcq.q: The most common cause of bacterial conjunctivitis in adults is
mcq.explanation: Staphylococcus aureus is the most common cause of bacterial conjunctivitis in adults. It is a Gram-positive coccus that is part of the normal flora of the skin.

mcq.q: Which of the following organisms causes trachoma?
mcq.explanation: Trachoma is caused by Chlamydia trachomatis (serotypes A, B, Ba, C). It is a chronic infection of the conjunctiva and cornea, leading to blindness.

mcq.q: Which of the following is NOT a feature of congenital CMV infection?
mcq.explanation: Congenital CMV infection is characterized by hepatosplenomegaly, jaundice, and microcephaly. Macrocephaly is not a feature.

mcq.q: Congenital rubella syndrome is caused by infection with rubella virus during
mcq.explanation: Congenital rubella syndrome occurs when rubella virus infection occurs during the first trimester of pregnancy. This is the period of maximal risk for fetal damage.

mcq.q: Which of the following is the most common cause of congenital deafness?
mcq.explanation: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) is the most common cause of congenital deafness. It can cause sensorineural hearing loss in affected infants.

mcq.q: The TORCH complex includes all of the following EXCEPT
mcq.explanation: The TORCH complex includes Toxoplasmosis, Other (syphilis, varicella), Rubella, Cytomegalovirus (CMV), and Herpes simplex virus (HSV). Hepatitis B is not part of the TORCH complex.

mcq.q: Congenital syphilis is characterized by all of the following EXCEPT
mcq.explanation: Congenital syphilis is characterized by snuffles, Hutchinson's teeth, and saddle nose. Hydrocephalus is not a characteristic feature.

mcq.q: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection in pregnant women can lead to
mcq.explanation: CMV infection in pregnant women can lead to congenital CMV infection, miscarriage, and stillbirth. It is a significant cause of congenital infections.

mcq.q: The classic triad of congenital toxoplasmosis includes all of the following EXCEPT
mcq.explanation: The classic triad of congenital toxoplasmosis includes chorioretinitis, hydrocephalus, and intracranial calcifications. Hepatosplenomegaly is not part of the classic triad.

mcq.q: The most common cause of congenital syphilis is
mcq.explanation: Congenital syphilis is caused by Treponema pallidum transmitted from mother to fetus. It can cause stillbirth, neonatal death, and a range of congenital anomalies.

mcq.q: Congenital rubella syndrome is characterized by all of the following EXCEPT
mcq.explanation: Congenital rubella syndrome is characterized by the classic triad of cataract, deafness, and heart defects. Hepatomegaly is not a typical feature.

mcq.q: Congenital toxoplasmosis is caused by
mcq.explanation: Congenital toxoplasmosis is caused by Toxoplasma gondii, a protozoan parasite. It is transmitted from mother to fetus during pregnancy.

mcq.q: Which of the following is the most common congenital infection?
mcq.explanation: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) is the most common congenital infection. It is transmitted from mother to fetus during pregnancy and can cause a wide range of congenital anomalies.

mcq.q: Which of the following oncogenic viruses is a DNA virus?
mcq.explanation: HPV is a DNA virus. HTLV-1 and HIV are RNA viruses (retroviruses). HCV is an RNA virus.

mcq.q: The association between HPV and cervical cancer is strongest with which HPV types?
mcq.explanation: HPV types 16 and 18 are the high-risk types most strongly associated with cervical cancer. They are responsible for approximately 70% of cervical cancers.

mcq.q: Hepatitis C virus (HCV) is associated with
mcq.explanation: Hepatitis C virus (HCV) is associated with hepatocellular carcinoma (liver cancer). It is a major cause of liver cancer worldwide.

mcq.q: All of the following are oncogenic viruses EXCEPT
mcq.explanation: Influenza virus is not an oncogenic virus. HPV, EBV, and HCV are well-known oncogenic viruses associated with various cancers.

mcq.q: Which of the following viruses is associated with Burkitt's lymphoma?
mcq.explanation: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) is associated with Burkitt's lymphoma, particularly the endemic form in Africa. It is a DNA virus that causes B-cell proliferation.

mcq.q: Kaposi's sarcoma is caused by
mcq.explanation: Kaposi's sarcoma is caused by Human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8), also known as Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV). It is commonly seen in immunocompromised patients, particularly those with AIDS.

mcq.q: Which of the following is an oncogenic RNA virus?
mcq.explanation: HTLV-1 is an oncogenic RNA virus (retrovirus) associated with adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma. It is transmitted through blood transfusion, sexual contact, and breast milk.

mcq.q: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) is associated with
mcq.explanation: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) is strongly associated with hepatocellular carcinoma (liver cancer). It is a major cause of liver cancer worldwide.

mcq.q: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) is associated with all of the following EXCEPT
mcq.explanation: EBV is associated with Burkitt's lymphoma, nasopharyngeal carcinoma, and Hodgkin's lymphoma. Kaposi's sarcoma is associated with Human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8).

mcq.q: Which of the following is the most common oncogenic virus?
mcq.explanation: HPV is the most common oncogenic virus, responsible for a significant proportion of cancers worldwide. It causes cervical, oropharyngeal, and anal cancers.

mcq.q: Human papilloma virus (HPV) is associated with which of the following cancers?
mcq.explanation: HPV is associated with cervical cancer, oropharyngeal cancer, anal cancer, and other anogenital cancers. HPV types 16 and 18 are the most oncogenic.

topics.name: Ch. 81: Zoonotic Infections: Plague, Tularemia and Bite Wound Infections

mcq.q: Which of the following is TRUE about Yersinia pestis?
mcq.answer: b) It is a Gram-negative coccobacillus
mcq.explanation: Yersinia pestis is a Gram-negative coccobacillus. It is the causative agent of plague and is transmitted by fleas.

mcq.q: Cat-scratch disease is caused by
mcq.explanation: Cat-scratch disease is caused by Bartonella henselae, a fastidious, Gram-negative bacillus. It is transmitted through cat scratches or bites.

mcq.q: Rat-bite fever is caused by
mcq.explanation: Rat-bite fever can be caused by Streptobacillus moniliformis (in North America) or Spirillum minus (in Asia). Both are transmitted through rat bites or scratches.

mcq.q: Which of the following is a zoonotic disease transmitted by animal bite?
mcq.explanation: Rabies, cat-scratch disease (Bartonella henselae), and rat-bite fever (Streptobacillus moniliformis or Spirillum minus) are all transmitted by animal bites or scratches.

mcq.q: The most common form of tularemia is
mcq.explanation: The ulceroglandular form is the most common form of tularemia. It presents with a skin ulcer and regional lymphadenopathy.

mcq.q: Tularemia is caused by
mcq.explanation: Tularemia (rabbit fever) is caused by Francisella tularensis, a Gram-negative coccobacillus. It is a zoonotic disease transmitted through contact with infected animals or tick bites.

mcq.q: The vector for bubonic plague is
mcq.explanation: Bubonic plague is transmitted by the rat flea (Xenopsylla cheopis). The organism multiplies in the flea's gut and is transmitted to humans through flea bites.

mcq.q: Plague is caused by
mcq.explanation: Plague is caused by Yersinia pestis, a Gram-negative coccobacillus. It is transmitted by fleas from infected rodents and causes three forms: bubonic, septicemic, and pneumonic.

mcq.q: Opportunistic infections are caused by
mcq.explanation: Opportunistic infections occur in immunocompromised hosts and are caused by organisms that normally do not cause disease in healthy individuals. These organisms take advantage of the weakened immune system.

mcq.q: Which of the following is the most common opportunistic infection in HIV/AIDS patients?
mcq.explanation: Pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonia (PCP) is the most common opportunistic infection in HIV/AIDS patients. It is caused by a fungus that typically affects immunocompromised individuals.

mcq.q: In renal transplant recipients, which organism is most likely to cause reactivation disease within 4 months after surgery? (PG Entrance 2020)
mcq.explanation: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) is a common cause of reactivation disease in renal transplant recipients, especially within the first few months after surgery. Immunosuppression increases the risk of CMV reactivation.

mcq.q: Nipah virus is classified as
mcq.explanation: Nipah virus is considered an emerging infectious disease. It is a zoonotic virus that emerged in Malaysia in 1998 and has since caused outbreaks in South Asia.

mcq.q: Which of the following is an emerging infectious disease?
mcq.explanation: SARS, COVID-19, and Ebola are all emerging infectious diseases. These diseases have appeared recently or have increased in incidence.

mcq.q: Which of the following is a Category A bioterrorism agent? (PG Entrance 2020)
mcq.explanation: Bacillus anthracis is classified as a Category A bioterrorism agent due to its potential for widespread impact and high mortality. Category A agents are the highest priority bioterrorism agents.

mcq.q: Oocysts of Cryptosporidium are best demonstrated by
mcq.explanation: Modified Ziehl-Neelsen (ZN) stain is most effective for demonstrating Cryptosporidium oocysts. This is a modified acid-fast stain that is used to detect the organism in stool samples.

mcq.q: A host that harbors the asexual stage of the parasite is known as
mcq.explanation: An intermediate host harbors the asexual stage of a parasite, whereas the definitive host harbors the sexual stage. This distinction is important in the life cycles of many parasites.

mcq.explanation: The loading dose depends on the volume of distribution. Formula: Loading dose = Desired plasma concentration x Volume of distribution.

mcq.explanation: Neostigmine is not commonly available in the form of a transdermal patch. Scopolamine, fentanyl, and clonidine are examples of drugs that can be administered via transdermal patches.

mcq.answer: c) Rectal is not a local route of drug administration.
mcq.explanation: Rectal administration is considered a systemic route because the drug can enter the systemic circulation, whereas topical, intra- articular, and intra- thecal are local routes.

mcq.q: The purpose of administration of a drug in the form of transdermal patch is

options.c: to maintain a constant drug level

mcq.answer: c) to maintain a constant drug level.
mcq.explanation: Transdermal patches are designed to provide a controlled and sustained release of a drug, helping to maintain a constant and therapeutic level of the medication in the bloodstream.
